sections.heading: Executive Overview
sections.body: Orion Systems Group delivered strong financial performance in FY2025, marked by broad-based revenue growth and meaningful margin expansion. Total revenue increased 14.8% year-over-year to $4.27 billion, supported by sustained demand for our subscription-based software platforms and improved execution across services. The strategic shift toward higher-margin recurring offerings continued to enhance earnings quality and cash generation. Management believes these results position the company for sustained profitable growth in FY2026.

sections.heading: Revenue Performance
sections.body: Software and subscription revenue grew 22% to $2.63 billion, representing 62% of consolidated revenue compared to 57% in FY2024. Professional services revenue rose 6% to $1.12 billion, driven by expanded enterprise deployments in North America and EMEA. Hardware and other revenue declined 3% to $520 million, reflecting our intentional deprioritization of lower-margin product lines. The increased mix of recurring software revenue materially improved revenue visibility entering the new fiscal year.

sections.heading: Profitability and Margins
sections.body: Operating income reached $812 million, up 19% from the prior year, resulting in an operating margin of 19.0%, compared to 18.2% in FY2024. Gross margin expanded 180 basis points to 64.5%, primarily due to higher software contribution and disciplined vendor cost management. Adjusted EBITDA totaled $1.02 billion, reflecting continued leverage on fixed operating expenses. Diluted earnings per share increased to $3.48, compared with $2.97 in the prior year.

sections.heading: Segment Highlights
sections.body: The Enterprise Cloud Solutions segment posted revenue of $2.11 billion, up 24%, driven by new multi-year SaaS contracts in the financial services and healthcare sectors. The Digital Infrastructure segment generated $1.34 billion in revenue, a 9% increase year-over-year, with stable margins despite pricing pressure in certain international markets. The Emerging Technologies segment contributed $820 million, reflecting 12% growth as AI-enabled analytics solutions gained traction. Each segment reported positive operating income for the full year.

sections.heading: Cash Flow and FY2026 Outlook
sections.body: Operating cash flow for FY2025 was $905 million, and free cash flow reached $744 million after capital expenditures of $161 million. The company reduced net debt by $210 million and ended the year with $1.3 billion in liquidity. For FY2026, management expects revenue growth between 10% and 12%, operating margin expansion of 50 to 100 basis points, and diluted EPS in the range of $3.85 to $4.05. Guidance assumes continued momentum in subscription bookings and stable macroeconomic conditions across core markets.

Fiscal Year 2025 Annual Performance Summary
For the Fiscal Year Ended 31 December 2025 | Orion Systems Group, Inc.

Section Executive Overview
Orion Systems Group delivered strong financial performance in FY2025, marked by broad-based revenue growth and meaningful margin expansion. Total revenue increased 14.8% year-over-year to $4.27 billion, supported by sustained demand for our subscription-based software platforms and improved execution across services. The strategic shift toward higher-margin recurring offerings continued to enhance earnings quality and cash generation. Management believes these results position the company for sustained profitable growth in FY2026.

Section Revenue Performance
Software and subscription revenue grew 22% to $2.63 billion, representing 62% of consolidated revenue compared to 57% in FY2024. Professional services revenue rose 6% to $1.12 billion, driven by expanded enterprise deployments in North America and EMEA. Hardware and other revenue declined 3% to $520 million, reflecting our intentional deprioritization of lower-margin product lines. The increased mix of recurring software revenue materially improved revenue visibility entering the new fiscal year.

Section Profitability and Margins
Operating income reached $812 million, up 19% from the prior year, resulting in an operating margin of 19.0%, compared to 18.2% in FY2024. Gross margin expanded 180 basis points to 64.5%, primarily due to higher software contribution and disciplined vendor cost management. Adjusted EBITDA totaled $1.02 billion, reflecting continued leverage on fixed operating expenses. Diluted earnings per share increased to $3.48, compared with $2.97 in the prior year.

Section Segment Highlights
The Enterprise Cloud Solutions segment posted revenue of $2.11 billion, up 24%, driven by new multi-year SaaS contracts in the financial services and healthcare sectors. The Digital Infrastructure segment generated $1.34 billion in revenue, a 9% increase year-over-year, with stable margins despite pricing pressure in certain international markets. The Emerging Technologies segment contributed $820 million, reflecting 12% growth as AI-enabled analytics solutions gained traction. Each segment reported positive operating income for the full year.

Section Cash Flow and FY2026 Outlook
Operating cash flow for FY2025 was $905 million, and free cash flow reached $744 million after capital expenditures of $161 million. The company reduced net debt by $210 million and ended the year with $1.3 billion in liquidity. For FY2026, management expects revenue growth between 10% and 12%, operating margin expansion of 50 to 100 basis points, and diluted EPS in the range of $3.85 to $4.05. Guidance assumes continued momentum in subscription bookings and stable macroeconomic conditions across core markets.

structure.full_text:
Fiscal Year 2025 Financial Results Overview
For the Year Ended 31 December 2025 | Issued: 18 February 2026 | Investor Relations Department

Section Executive Summary
Fiscal Year 2025 marked a year of broad-based growth and measurable margin expansion across all operating segments. Total revenue increased to $4.87 billion, representing 13.4% growth compared to FY2024, driven primarily by expansion in recurring software subscriptions and enterprise renewals. Operating income rose 22% year over year to $812 million, reflecting disciplined cost execution and improved product mix. Management believes these results position the company to sustain profitable growth into FY2026.

Section Revenue Performance
Recurring software and cloud services revenue grew 19% to $2.96 billion and now accounts for 61% of total company revenue, up from 57% in the prior year. Professional services revenue increased 7% to $1.14 billion, supported by higher implementation volumes in North America and Western Europe. Hardware and ancillary product sales remained stable at $770 million, reflecting strategic prioritization of higher-margin offerings. Annual recurring revenue (ARR) exited the year at $3.21 billion, an increase of $465 million year over year.

Section Margins and Cost Structure
Gross margin improved to 68.5%, up 240 basis points from FY2024, driven by a higher mix of subscription-based software and operational efficiencies in service delivery. Operating margin expanded to 16.7%, compared to 15.3% in the prior year, as selling, general and administrative expenses grew at a slower pace than revenue. The company realized $54 million in structural cost savings through vendor consolidation and automation initiatives. Research and development investment increased 9% to $426 million, supporting continued innovation while maintaining overall margin discipline.

Section Earnings and Cash Flow
Diluted earnings per share for FY2025 were $2.84, compared to $2.21 in FY2024, reflecting higher operating income and a modest reduction in share count from the company’s repurchase program. Net income totaled $598 million, up 24% year over year. Operating cash flow reached $905 million, enabling capital expenditures of $138 million and share repurchases totaling $210 million. The company ended the year with $1.12 billion in cash and equivalents and a net leverage ratio of 1.1x.

Section Segment Highlights and FY2026 Outlook
The Enterprise Solutions segment delivered 17% revenue growth and achieved an operating margin of 21%, supported by strong demand in regulated industries. The Mid-Market and SMB segment grew 11%, driven by digital channel expansion and improved renewal rates. For FY2026, management projects total revenue growth in the range of 10% to 12%, operating margin between 17.5% and 18.5%, and diluted EPS of $3.05 to $3.20. Guidance assumes continued momentum in recurring software, stable macroeconomic conditions, and ongoing cost discipline.

Full-year revenue was $12.4B total for FY2025 ended December 31, 2025, reflecting continued top-line resilience in a mixed macro environment. Operating margin expanded to 18.6% in FY2025, up from 16.9% in FY2024, and diluted earnings per share increased to $4.12 in FY2025 from $3.58 in FY2024, underscoring positive operating leverage.

Margin improvement of 170 basis points versus FY2024 reflects disciplined cost management, productivity gains in manufacturing and services, and targeted SG&A optimization initiatives executed through 2025. These actions improved operating efficiency without material capital intensity, enabling margin expansion while preserving investment in strategic growth areas and maintaining flexibility to fund priority projects in 2026.

Our capital allocation in FY2025 prioritized shareholder returns and balance sheet strength. The Board authorized continued dividends and share repurchases under the existing program, supporting per-share value alongside the company’s commitment to disciplined return metrics. The company remains committed to maintaining an investment-grade profile, prudent leverage, and transparent reporting to investors and analysts through 2026. It will also evaluate opportunistic M&A when aligned with shareholder value creation.

structure.heading: Segment Performance Drivers and FY2026 Investor Guidance Framework
text_content: **Segment Performance Drivers and FY2026 Investor Guidance Framework**

Cloud & Subscription revenue increased 22% year over year to $5.6B in FY2025, driven by enterprise renewals, expansion within existing accounts, and accelerated adoption of our Enterprise Cloud Platform. International revenue represented 41% of FY2025 total revenue, reflecting strong growth across EMEA and APAC and targeted go-to-market investments implemented during the fiscal year. Product-led upsell programs and multi-year contracts increased average contract value and improved visibility, while channel partnerships expanded reach in mid-market segments. These dynamics established momentum entering FY2026 planning. This momentum underpins our commercial priorities.

Segment-level margin performance reflected contrasting dynamics: subscription-based software delivered higher recurring gross margins, while professional services and one-time implementation engagements continued to carry lower incremental margins. During FY2025 we executed targeted cost-to-serve optimizations, standardized delivery platforms, and automated billing and provisioning, which together reduced variable delivery costs and improved throughput. Sales efficiency and renewals discipline tightened customer acquisition costs. These actions improved segment margin contribution and created levers that management expects to scale into FY2026 without material dilution of R&D investment or customer success capacity further.

For FY2026 we are issuing investor guidance that targets revenue of $13.2B–$13.6B and an operating margin of 19.0%–19.8%. This guidance assumes continued subscription momentum, stable foreign exchange versus current rates, mid-single-digit growth in EMEA and APAC, and execution of announced cost efficiency programs. The framework communicates key performance indicators, including ARR growth, renewal rates, and contribution margin by segment, and establishes scenario-based sensitivities for upside and downside cases. We will update progress on the quarterly earnings call and maintain engagement with investors through our investor relations team.
